chapter.title: Listening Section
chapter.source: ETS — TOEFL iBT® Practice Test 2 (aligned with tests from January 21, 2026)

summary: Listening section of the official ETS Practice Test 2, in two modules. Module 1: Choose a Response (1–8), two conversations (9–12), a club announcement (13–14) and a physics talk (15–18). Module 2: Choose a Response (1–8), a conversation (9–10), a campus radio announcement (11–12) and an environmental science talk (13–16). The audio is the ETS recordings; transcripts are hidden until you reveal them. Answers come from the ETS answer keys (PDF pp. 26–27).

passage.title: Module 1 · Choose the best response
passage.text: Listen to each statement once, then pick the best reply. The statement is shown after you answer.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 1. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: The lighter one is over there.
There's a switch on the back wall.
I prefer to work at home.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: There's a switch on the back wall.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “How can I get this light to work?” — Answer key: (B) There's a switch on the back wall.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 2. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: Let's try to get there early.
What's a better day for you?
It's not on my schedule either.
I was in a meeting last night.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: What's a better day for you?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “I'm not available tomorrow.” — Answer key: (B) What's a better day for you?

multiple_choice_questions.question: 3. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: I can hold that for you.
Stage lighting is usually very hot.
My roommate is a talented basketball player.
Do you know who the judges will be?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Do you know who the judges will be?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “The campus talent contest will be held next Saturday evening.” — Answer key: (D) Do you know who the judges will be?

multiple_choice_questions.question: 4. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: Don't worry about it—I'll get him.
He said he prefers the window seat.
The station now has a snack shop.
There's road construction near the entrance.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Don't worry about it—I'll get him.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “What time do I need to pick up Michael from the train station?” — Answer key: (A) Don't worry about it—I'll get him.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 5. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Yes, it is.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “Isn't the grocery store open late tonight?” — Answer key: (A) Yes, it is.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 6. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: They are in the blue folder.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: They are in the blue folder.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “Did you bring the identification documents?” — Answer key: (A) They are in the blue folder.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 7. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: No, it's tonight.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Wait, isn't the concert tomorrow night?” — Answer key: (A) No, it's tonight.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 8. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Well, I understand.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “I'm not available this afternoon.” — Answer key: (D) Well, I understand.

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to a conversation
passage.transcript:
Man: I think my laptop is acting up again. It keeps freezing and shutting down randomly.
Woman: That’s frustrating. Have you tried restarting it or running a virus scan?
Man: Yes, I did both, but it didn’t help. I might need to take it to a repair shop.
Woman: That sounds like a good idea. They should be able to diagnose and fix the issue.
Man: I’ll do that this afternoon.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 9. What problem is the man experiencing with his laptop?
choices: It keeps freezing and shutting down.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: It keeps freezing and shutting down.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) It keeps freezing and shutting down.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 10. What will the man most likely do next?
choices: Take his laptop to a repair shop
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Take his laptop to a repair shop
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) Take his laptop to a repair shop

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to a conversation
passage.transcript:
Man: Are you going to the supermarket today by any chance?
Woman: I was just there yesterday. Why?
Man: I suddenly remembered that I’m supposed to bring some drinks to my team’s lunch meeting tomorrow at work, and I’m in the middle of a project I need to finish tonight.
Woman: You’re in luck. I stocked up yesterday.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 11. What is the man’s problem?
choices: He has nothing to eat for lunch.
He is unable to attend a meeting.
He forgot about an obligation at work.
He needs more resources to finish a project.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: He forgot about an obligation at work.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) He forgot about an obligation at work.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 12. What does the woman imply when she says, “I stocked up yesterday”?
choices: She does not plan to go to work tomorrow.
She will provide the man with drinks for his meeting.
The supermarket has plenty of drinks available.
The man will not need extra time to finish his project.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: She will provide the man with drinks for his meeting.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) She will provide the man with drinks for his meeting.

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to an announcement at a university club meeting
passage.transcript: Announcer: Welcome to the creative writing club's monthly meeting! Before we get started, I wanted to remind you of the guidelines for our upcoming short-story contest. We’re looking for stories on the theme of family, and all stories must be submitted by the end of November to be considered. Good luck to everyone participating!
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 13. Why does the speaker mention family?
choices: It is the topic of the story they are reading.
It was discussed at last month’s meeting.
Families are invited to the next meeting.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: It is a contest theme.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) It is a contest theme.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 14. What does the speaker encourage the participants to do?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Observe the guidelines
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) Observe the guidelines

passage.title: Module 1 · Listen to a talk in a physics class
passage.transcript:
Professor: Dark matter is a type of matter that doesn’t emit, absorb, or reflect light, making it invisible to current instruments. Despite being unobservable directly, it’s believed to make up about 27 percent of the universe’s mass-energy content. How do scientists know dark matter exists? Well, all the stars in a galaxy rotate around the center of their galaxy. According to basic physics, the farther a star is from the center of a galaxy, the slower it should rotate. However, observations show that stars in the outer regions of galaxies rotate at unexpectedly high speeds. This anomaly suggests that a massive, unseen matter is exerting gravitational force, keeping the stars moving faster than expected.

Dark matter is hugely important for the structure of the universe. Computer simulations show that galaxies wouldn't have formed the way they did if dark matter hadn't been around. But what does dark matter consist of? Well, there are different theories, so let's consider a couple of them.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 15. What is the main topic of the talk?
choices: Material in the universe that cannot be directly seen
The distribution of stars in galaxies
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Material in the universe that cannot be directly seen
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) Material in the universe that cannot be directly seen

multiple_choice_questions.question: 16. According to the speaker, how do scientists infer the existence of dark matter?
choices: From the temperature of visible matter
From the amount of light in the universe
From the number of stars in galaxies
From the speed of stars' movement
multiple_choice_questions.answer: From the speed of stars' movement
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (D) From the speed of stars' movement

multiple_choice_questions.question: 17. Why does the speaker mention computer simulations?
choices: To support the claim that dark matter plays an important role in the universe
To describe how the gravitational forces acting on stars were calculated
To highlight the anomalies in basic physics
To explain how the speeds of stars were measured
multiple_choice_questions.answer: To support the claim that dark matter plays an important role in the universe
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) To support the claim that dark matter plays an important role in the universe

multiple_choice_questions.question: 18. What will the speaker most likely discuss next?
choices: Measurements of dark matter in galaxies
The anomalies in galaxy rotation caused by dark matter
The distribution of dark matter in the universe
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Ideas about dark matter’s composition
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) Ideas about dark matter’s composition

passage.title: Module 2 · Choose the best response
passage.text: Listen to each statement once, then pick the best reply. The statement is shown after you answer.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 1. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: I'm not sure.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “Who is responsible for the project timeline?” — Answer key: (B) I'm not sure.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 2. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Actually, it was rescheduled.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “Why did the team meeting get canceled?” — Answer key: (C) Actually, it was rescheduled.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 3. Listen, then choose the best response.
choices: Let me know what you think.
What exactly do you need help with?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: What exactly do you need help with?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Can you assist me with my science report?” — Answer key: (C) What exactly do you need help with?

multiple_choice_questions.question: 4. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: That's unfortunate.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “I'm not sure about the current plan.” — Answer key: (A) That's unfortunate.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 5. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: That's what I'll do.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “If you need help, ask Ms. Johnson.” — Answer key: (C) That's what I'll do.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 6. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: At 1 p.m.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Woman: “What time does the event start?” — Answer key: (B) At 1 p.m.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 7. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: The marketing team is.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Who is hosting the party tonight?” — Answer key: (A) The marketing team is.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 8. Listen, then choose the best response.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Have you checked the weather?
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Man: “Let's go hiking this weekend.” — Answer key: (C) Have you checked the weather?

passage.title: Module 2 · Listen to a conversation
passage.transcript:
Man: Have you returned the books we borrowed from the library?
Woman: Why? I thought we could keep them for six weeks.
Man: Actually, it’s now four weeks. They changed the policy. I guess I forgot to tell you!
Woman: That means they’re due tomorrow!
Man: Exactly!
Woman: In that case, I’ll take care of it right now!
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 9. What was the woman not aware of?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: The library’s borrowing policy
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (B) The library’s borrowing policy

multiple_choice_questions.question: 10. What will the woman probably do next?
choices: Make a phone call to the library
Pay a fine for returning books late
Borrow a new book from the library
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Return books to the library
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) Return books to the library

passage.title: Module 2 · Listen to an announcement on the campus radio station
passage.transcript: Announcer: Good evening everyone. Just a friendly reminder that the university's annual charity auction will take place tomorrow at 7 P.M. in the Main Hall. All proceeds will go to local charities. We hope to see you there and appreciate your support!
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 11. What is the main topic of the announcement?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: An upcoming fundraiser
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (D) An upcoming fundraiser

multiple_choice_questions.question: 12. What does the speaker hope the listeners will do?
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Attend an event
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) Attend an event

passage.title: Module 2 · Listen to a talk in an environmental science class
passage.transcript:
Professor: Biomimicry is the human practice of learning from and imitating things found in nature in order to create new inventions. This way, scientists and engineers can create innovative solutions that are both efficient and sustainable.

One well-known example of biomimicry is the development of a widely used fastening system. The inventor was inspired by the way burrs, uh thorns, from plants stuck to his dog’s fur. By replicating the tiny hooks found on the burrs he removed from the dog fur, he created the new fastening system.

Another example is the design of energy-efficient buildings based on the ventilation system of structures created by termites. Termites are ground-dwelling insects that use different materials to create hills, or mounds, in which the termites live. Termite mounds have a complex network of vents. The vents maintain a stable internal temperature, which can be emulated in human architecture.

Biomimicry can also be applied to renewable energy. For instance, researchers are developing wind turbine blades modeled after the flippers of humpback whales. The unique shape of the flippers reduces drag and increases efficiency, leading to more effective wind energy capture.
passage.text: Listen first (once, as on test day), then answer. Reveal the transcript only when reviewing.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 13. What is the talk mainly about?
choices: Ways in which humans use natural materials in clothing and architecture
New methods of using renewable energy
Examples of how humans imitate nature for practical purposes
multiple_choice_questions.answer: Examples of how humans imitate nature for practical purposes
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (D) Examples of how humans imitate nature for practical purposes

multiple_choice_questions.question: 14. Why does the speaker mention a dog?
choices: To illustrate how an inventor copied animal behavior
To compare its efficiency in movement with that of humpback whales
To explain how a structure found in plants inspired an invention
To show the close bond between scientists and animals
multiple_choice_questions.answer: To explain how a structure found in plants inspired an invention
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (C) To explain how a structure found in plants inspired an invention

multiple_choice_questions.question: 15. What point does the speaker make about termite mounds?
choices: The temperature inside of them does not change much.
Termites sometimes build them near human-made structures.
Building them takes a lot of energy.
They are created mostly from plant material.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: The temperature inside of them does not change much.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (A) The temperature inside of them does not change much.

multiple_choice_questions.question: 16. What does the speaker imply about wind turbine blades that are being developed?
choices: The noise they create can be harmful to whales.
They can be easily installed on buildings.
They can be efficiently constructed from renewable materials.
They are very similar to some whales' flippers in shape.
multiple_choice_questions.answer: They are very similar to some whales' flippers in shape.
multiple_choice_questions.explanation: Answer key: (D) They are very similar to some whales' flippers in shape.
